chapters.title: The Terminal Learned to Talk
chapters.tease: Autocomplete finishes your sentence; an agent finishes your task. Here is what that difference asks of you.

chapters.title: A Short History of a Fast Year
chapters.tease: Twenty months from research preview to a family of doors: how to keep up without chasing every change.

chapters.title: Gather, Act, Verify
chapters.tease: Every session, grand or trivial, runs one loop. See it and you can steer it; miss it and the agent looks like a magician.

chapters.title: Installing Without Ceremony
chapters.tease: Installation should take the least of your time. Choose the route you will forget about, then forget about it.

chapters.title: Your First Five Minutes
chapters.tease: One explanation, one small change, one honest review, one commit. The whole shape of the work, in five minutes.

chapters.title: Tools Are the Hands
chapters.tease: A model alone can only produce text. Its tools are its hands, and their names are the handles for permission.

chapters.title: Choosing a Mind
chapters.tease: The right model is the cheapest one that does the job well. Pick the mind by the task, not by vanity.

chapters.title: Paying for the Privilege
chapters.tease: Most waste is not caused by a big model. It is caused by vague requests. Spend attention before tokens.

chapters.title: What It Is Bad At
chapters.tease: It is often wrong in the same calm, fluent voice it uses when it is right. Learn the four shapes of failure.

chapters.title: Delegation, Not Autocomplete
chapters.tease: You stopped being the typist. You are still, and always, the one who says it is finished.

chapters.title: The Terminal Is the Source
chapters.tease: Many front doors, one house. The terminal has the fewest decorations, which makes it the best place to learn the building.

chapters.title: The Desktop App
chapters.tease: For the window people: visual diffs, parallel sessions in their own worktrees, and chores that run while you supervise.

chapters.title: Claude Code on the Web
chapters.tease: A fresh machine for every session, in a container you can close the laptop on. One rule: push, or it never happened.

chapters.title: Environments and Setup Scripts
chapters.tease: A cloud container is a guest house that knows nothing about you. Environments stock it before the guest arrives.

chapters.title: In the Editor
chapters.tease: Some work wants distance and some wants proximity. The editor puts the diff where the code already is.

chapters.title: In Your Pocket
chapters.tease: The phone is a remote, not a workbench. Good for starting, following and nudging; bad for bearing the weight of judgement.

chapters.title: Remote Control
chapters.tease: Cloud sessions are tidy but they are not your machine. Remote Control keeps the work at home and lets you steer from anywhere.

chapters.title: A Colleague in Slack
chapters.tease: The export is broken again, says the channel, followed by emoji. The conversation is already the ticket; now someone can pick it up.

chapters.title: Hands in the Browser
chapters.tease: Some work lives behind a login with no API. Claude in Chrome uses your real browser, so lend it as you would lend keys.

chapters.title: Choosing the Right Door
chapters.tease: Eight doors and one menu written in reassuring adjectives. Ask in order: where the work is, where you are, how closely you watch.

chapters.title: Say What Done Looks Like
chapters.tease: Most bad sessions begin with a good intention and a bad sentence. A wish has no edges; the agent will find some for you.

chapters.title: Plan Before You Cut
chapters.tease: The expensive mistakes happen in the first five minutes, before a line is written. Plan mode is insurance that costs reading time.

chapters.title: How Much Rope
chapters.tease: Six permission modes from cautious to reckless. Trust is not a feeling; it is the size of the mess if the agent is wrong.

chapters.title: The Undo Button Is Real
chapters.tease: Every edit is snapshotted. Rewind code, conversation or both, and suddenly letting it try the bold version first costs a keypress.

chapters.title: Context Is a Budget
chapters.tease: Every token in the window is spent. A single verbose test run can outweigh the module you were trying to fix.

chapters.title: The Art of Forgetting
chapters.tease: The ancient schools built memory palaces but never shared a window with four hundred lines of build output. Learn to let go.

chapters.title: Interrupting Gracefully
chapters.tease: Watching an agent work is like watching someone parallel park your car. Occasionally you see the bollard first.

chapters.title: Make It Prove It
chapters.tease: An agent that says it has finished is offering an opinion. An agent that ran the tests is offering evidence.

chapters.title: Thinking Out Loud
chapters.tease: Maximum effort on a typo is a committee choosing a sandwich. Low effort on a race condition is a Friday in production.

chapters.title: Show, Don't Describe
chapters.tease: The button looks a bit off on mobile. Paste the screenshot instead. A paraphrase of an error is a rumour about an error.

chapters.title: A Letter to Your Successor
chapters.tease: Every session arrives clever, well read and entirely ignorant of your project. You could tell it each morning. You will tire by Wednesday.

chapters.title: The Memory Hierarchy
chapters.tease: There is not one memory file. There are several, stacked like an old town, and knowing which layer to write in is the skill.

chapters.title: Let It Write the First Draft
chapters.tease: You know too much about your project to see it clearly. Let a reader who has never seen the house draft the note, then cut.

chapters.title: It Takes Its Own Notes
chapters.tease: You are not the only one writing things down. Claude keeps a notebook, and an unpruned memory is a rumour with a filing system.

chapters.title: Settings Have Scopes
chapters.tease: Memory tells Claude what to know. Settings tell Claude Code how to behave, and unlike memory, the layers compete. One wins.

chapters.title: Allow, Ask, Deny
chapters.tease: The first time it asks to run the tests, be glad. The fortieth time you click yes without reading, which is worse than never asking.

chapters.title: Environment and Model Defaults
chapters.tease: Which model to start with, which variables every session needs: boring choices that belong in a file, not in your head.

chapters.title: A Voice of Its Own
chapters.tease: The same engineer can be a brisk colleague or a patient teacher. Output styles change the manner without changing the competence.

chapters.title: Making It Yours
chapters.tease: A tool you use for hours each day is closer to furniture than software, and furniture should fit. Fix only the friction you can name.

chapters.title: Policy From Above
chapters.tease: When thousands of people run an agent against company code, someone sets the floor. Managed settings are a floor nobody below can lower.

chapters.title: The Slash Commands Worth Knowing
chapters.tease: A kitchen holds forty utensils and you cook with four. Here are the four, and where the rest hang when the soufflé collapses.

chapters.title: Your Own Commands
chapters.tease: Every team has phrases it types forty times a month. Typing them again is not diligence; it is a tax you stopped noticing.

chapters.title: Skills Are Recipes
chapters.tease: A recipe is one dish written down by someone who knows where it goes wrong. A skill is that, for Claude.

chapters.title: Anatomy of a SKILL.md
chapters.tease: A skill file has an envelope and a page. The frontmatter decides when, the body decides how, and the shelf decides how much.

chapters.title: Progressive Disclosure
chapters.tease: A library does not read you every book when you walk in. It shows you the spines. Skills work the same way.

chapters.title: The Description Is the Trigger
chapters.tease: A handful of words decide whether the rest are ever read. Write the description badly and your skill is a book with no spine label.

chapters.title: Plugins Are Parcels
chapters.tease: Skills, commands, a subagent and a hook scattered like tools on a garage floor. None is easy to hand over. A plugin is the box.

chapters.title: The Marketplace
chapters.tease: A marketplace sounds grander than it is: a well-labelled shelf of plugins. Easy to get from, not automatically safe to keep from.

chapters.title: Sharing With the Team
chapters.tease: The best thing you can do for a team is make the good habits arrive with git clone. Not a wiki page.

chapters.title: A Library of Habits
chapters.tease: Nobody designs a bench in a weekend. It accretes, one solved irritation at a time. Your skills are your judgement, written down.

chapters.title: Promises the Harness Keeps
chapters.tease: Instructions are what you hope will happen. Hooks are what you have arranged. The model does not get a vote.

chapters.title: The Event Catalogue
chapters.tease: A hook is only as useful as its timing. Learn the clock first; the cleverness is mostly choosing the right minute.

chapters.title: The Bouncer at PreToolUse
chapters.tease: Every club has a person at the door whose job is not to be liked. The one point where a no costs nothing.

chapters.title: Tidy Up After Yourself
chapters.tease: Claude writes decent code and indifferent whitespace. Stop asking for the formatter and arrange for it to run.

chapters.title: Not Finished Yet
chapters.tease: The most expensive sentence in agentic coding is Done, all changes complete. A Stop hook moves the discovery back to where it is cheapest.

chapters.title: Morning Briefing
chapters.tease: Every session begins in innocent ignorance. Which branch, what changed, is the database up. A twenty-line script can say it for you.

chapters.title: Exit Codes and JSON
chapters.tease: Hooks speak to the harness in a deliberately small vocabulary. Small vocabularies are hard to misunderstand.

chapters.title: The Sandbox
chapters.tease: Hooks catch moments. The sandbox changes the room. A regex is a fence; the operating system is a wall.

chapters.title: Data Is Not Instructions
chapters.tease: Web pages, issues, dependency readmes and tool results: text you did not write, some of which has learned to speak in the imperative.

chapters.title: Security Review Before Merge
chapters.tease: One guardrail sits at the boundary that matters most: the moment code leaves your branch and becomes everyone's problem.

chapters.title: A Universal Socket
chapters.tease: Out of the box, Claude can touch what your terminal can touch. A great deal, and a small room. MCP adds the doors.

chapters.title: Adding a Server
chapters.tease: Fitting a server takes one command in two shapes. Then check, because a registered server and a working server are different things.

chapters.title: Scopes and .mcp.json
chapters.tease: Every server lives somewhere, and where it lives decides who else gets it. A config file should describe the lock, never contain the key.

chapters.title: Logging In Politely
chapters.tease: A tracker will not hand over tickets to any process that asks nicely. Sign in through the browser, and no password touches a file.

chapters.title: Resources and Prompts
chapters.tease: Tools get the attention because tools do things. Resources and prompts are the quieter help, and most people never open either menu.

chapters.title: Tool Search
chapters.tease: Five servers, two hundred tool definitions, and a context window to protect. Knowing where the book is kept is nearly as good as carrying it.

chapters.title: Connectors in the Cloud
chapters.tease: In the cloud, much of the plugging in is done for you. Connectors are keys set once in your account, used while you sleep.

chapters.title: Building Your Own Server
chapters.tease: Most of the time you should not build a server. Then there is the pricing service nobody outside the building has heard of.

chapters.title: Too Many Tools
chapters.tease: Everyone goes through the phase: a dozen servers in a fortnight. Tool search saves your context, not your judgement.

chapters.title: The World, Plugged In
chapters.tease: On one side, an agent that talks. On the other, an agent that does. MCP is the boundary, and you place it.

chapters.title: Specialists With Clean Desks
chapters.tease: The answer you wanted was six lines. The mess it left was six thousand. A subagent works at a clean desk.

chapters.title: Writing an Agent
chapters.tease: The third time you type the same careful brief, you are doing clerical work a file could do. Write the brief once.

chapters.title: The Built-in Crew
chapters.tease: Before you write a single agent, Claude Code already has staff. Three built-ins you will meet in transcripts before you think to ask.

chapters.title: Work in the Background
chapters.tease: A nine-minute suite takes nine minutes because it does. Sitting and watching is a poor use of a session and a worse use of you.

chapters.title: One Repo, Many Desks
chapters.tease: Two people editing the same file is a comedy. Two Claude sessions doing it is the same comedy, faster. Each session needs its own desk.

chapters.title: Running a Small Team
chapters.tease: Around the second coffee, one session no longer feels like enough. Run as many as you can review well, and not one more.

chapters.title: Headless and Scriptable
chapters.tease: Some of Claude Code's most useful work happens with nobody watching at all. Print mode makes it a well-behaved Unix citizen on a short leash.

chapters.title: The Agent SDK
chapters.tease: The loop, the tools, the permissions: not magic welded into a terminal program. A harness, and Anthropic ships it as a library.

chapters.title: Workflows at Scale
chapters.tease: Two hundred test files to migrate: a fortnight by hand, a full context window by file thirty. As a workflow, fan out, verify each, collect.

chapters.title: When Not to Parallelise
chapters.tease: After nine chapters on doing several things at once, the unfashionable part: much of the time, you should not.

chapters.title: Claude on GitHub
chapters.tease: Most of a team's work waits in the long grey corridor of GitHub. Put Claude where the waiting is.

chapters.title: Review Before Merge
chapters.tease: Code review is the oldest quality gate and the most skipped. Nobody skips it on purpose; it loses to Thursday afternoon and arrives as LGTM.

chapters.title: Driving a PR to Green
chapters.tease: Opening a pull request feels like finishing. It is the start of a small, tedious siege, and a session can hold it for you.

chapters.title: Routines
chapters.tease: Some prompts you type every Monday in slightly different words with slightly less enthusiasm. That kind wants to become a routine.

chapters.title: The Loop
chapters.tease: Sometimes you need a thing checked every few minutes for an hour, then stopped. Subscribe if you can, loop if you must.

chapters.title: Projects and Threads
chapters.tease: A team's work is many conversations, half about the same thing, most forgotten by Wednesday. Projects give that sprawl a shape.

chapters.title: Artifacts and Documents
chapters.tease: A great deal of what Claude produces dies in the scrollback. If the work was meant for anyone else, it was not finished, merely done.

chapters.title: Teams and Enterprise
chapters.tease: For an individual, Claude Code is a tool. For an organisation it is a policy question, answered by someone who will never see your terminal.

chapters.title: Watching the Meter
chapters.tease: The question about cost usually arrives as a chart from finance with a line going up and no explanation of what was bought.

chapters.title: Rolling It Out
chapters.tease: The first developer to use Claude Code has a wonderful week. The tenth has a confusing one. The difference is what nobody wrote down.

chapters.title: Spec First
chapters.tease: Most failed sessions fail before the first edit. Someone typed add billing, and three hundred lines later both parties were imagining different features.

chapters.title: Tests as the Contract
chapters.tease: An agent will tell you it has finished, with complete sincerity. Sincerity is not evidence. A test is.

chapters.title: Archaeology
chapters.tease: Every codebase older than eighteen months is a dig site. You have been asked to change something in it by Friday. Record before you remove.

chapters.title: Not Only for Coders
chapters.tease: Claude Code is a coding tool roughly the way a kitchen is a place for boiling water. Most working life is files in a folder.

chapters.title: Restraint Is a Feature
chapters.tease: In the second week everything becomes possible, so everything gets attempted. The bill, in money or evenings, arrives later and is unsentimental.

chapters.title: A Field Guide to Failure
chapters.tease: Agents fail in a small number of recognisable ways. Learn the species and you stop being surprised. Surprise is expensive; recognition is cheap.

chapters.title: Your Job After the Agent
chapters.tease: When the typing goes, an uncomfortable question arrives: what exactly were you for? The answer is not nothing, and it is not prompting.

chapters.title: A Day in 2026
chapters.tease: Seven-forty, phone in hand, reading what the night produced. Count the minutes typing code today: perhaps forty. Count the decisions: dozens.

chapters.title: What Comes Next
chapters.tease: Any chapter about the future of a tool that changes monthly is written in pencil. Learn the right layer.

chapters.title: Delegate the Work, Keep the Judgement
chapters.tease: The whole book in six words: delegate the work, keep the judgement. Everything else is machinery for doing that well.
